correctness.rationale: The single-cycle incidence kernel gives an affine isomorphism B from bridge cube [-1/2,1/2]^(n-k) times the zero-sum projection of the k-cube. Balanced mixed cycle-sign patterns have maximal projected squared norm floor(k^2/4)/k; uniform balanced cycles and independent bridge signs form a centered isotropic contact distribution for the two-block shape S with eigenvalues d/4 and d floor(k^2/4)/(k(k-1)). The averaging-trace/AM–GM certificate establishes global uniqueness of the Löwner ellipsoid. B S B^T equals stated weighted Laplacian; pseudo-determinant BB^T=n k follows from matrix-tree theorem and yields exact volume and contact count. Exact consecutive-length ratio formulas and Bernoulli prove strict volume increase at fixed n. Verified odd/even cases and bridge independence.

evidence: Gassmann–Althoff full thesis-hosted PDF treats conservative ellipsoid bounds for general redundant generators and exact nonredundant generator case; Padrol et al. describe graphical deformation cones and combinatorics.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General techniques do not supply optimality for redundant one-circuit generators, explicit weight ratio or contact distribution as a corollary; the submitted certificate is additional mathematics.

value.rationale: The exact Euclidean Löwner ellipsoid is a fundamental natural convex-geometric invariant of graphical zonotopes. The one-circuit family is a geometrically motivated first non-parallelotope class, and exact contact classes and cycle-dependent sharp volume extremizers are useful, mathematically nontrivial structural information. The all-unicyclic solution is not an arbitrary small graph census or a generic method restatement.

limitations: Connected unweighted simple graph with exactly one cycle in canonical Euclidean incidence embedding; no general multicycle or arbitrary weighted graph extension.
